stemMd: A researcher wants to estimate heat experienced by people walking their usual routes. Which approach best matches the passage?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Use only shaded doorways because they are easy to access.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Assume identical exposure whenever neighbourhood names match.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Sample relevant routes and times rather than relying solely on standardized open sites.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Use the single coolest reading as the city estimate.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Ignore the timing of pedestrians’ walks.

explanationMd: A measurement design should match the target experience. Route and time sampling aligns observations with pedestrian exposure.

distractorRationale.a: Convenience locations may not represent usual routes.
distractorRationale.d: An extreme does not represent the exposure distribution.
distractorRationale.e: Time is part of the stated sampling population.
